news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

This stellar new discovery needed some “space” before revealing itself.

Scientists have long struggled to map the region of space beyond Pluto, relying on scattered discoveries and indirect clues from other planets’ movements.

Now, researchers have announced a new discovery from the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, high atop Cerro Pachón in Chile.

A large object in the Kuiper Belt — a distant region of icy and rocky bodies past Neptune — appears to be a new candidate dwarf planet. Named 2026 ED138, its entire orbit lies within Pluto’s distance range from the Sun, yet it was only just discovered.

The Rubin Observatory features the largest digital camera ever built for astronomy, capable of capturing a patch of sky equal to 40 full moons in a single shot. The telescope first saw light in June 2025, and by March 2026, the object entered its field of view. Since then, the team traced it through 30 detections across 20 nights of Rubin observations, dating from 4 March to 11 July 2026.

The light turned out to be one of the largest objects ever discovered past Neptune, potentially rivaling the size of other above-average dwarf planets, such as Makemake and Haumea.

Astrophysicist Matthew Holman of the Harvard-Smithsonian Center spotted the object on Oct. 13, 2026, while analyzing Rubin observations using software developed with colleague Kevin Napier.

Searching older data, the team found the object in images from the Dark Energy Camera dating back to February 2016. The camera had also captured it in 2017, 2018, 2019, and 2023. Holman noted that objects like this are “very rare.” Double-checking his work in “excited disbelief,” he made sure no errors had been made.

The region beyond Neptune begins roughly 30 astronomical units (AU) from the Sun, and everything we know suggests far more remains hidden. The Kuiper Belt extends out to 55 AU, beyond which lies the theoretical Oort Cloud.

Thousands of objects past Neptune hint at materials in even more distant reaches. Spotting them is extraordinarily difficult because they reflect very little sunlight and appear faint to telescopes.

They are also extremely cold, giving off very little heat radiation (infrared light) for sensors to pick up.

If 2026 ED138 is on the larger end of size estimates, it could rank alongside other dwarf planets — meaning its own gravity would be strong enough to pull it into a round shape. The finding shows Rubin’s ability to repeatedly scan swaths of the sky and pick out faint, slow-moving bodies that earlier surveys missed — and reveal objects hiding in plain sight.

According to the Minor Planet Center, ED138 takes about 281 years to orbit the Sun, ranging from 36.86 Astronomical Units (AU) at its closest approach to 49.04 AU at its farthest.

Its orbit is also tilted by roughly 24.5 degrees relative to the rest of the solar system — a prime example of the orbital quirks that make these objects so hard to track. Most planets sit on a relatively flat, disc-like plane called the ecliptic. Because of this, astronomers focus the majority of their telescopes on this narrow band of the sky.

An object tilted by 24.5 degrees spends most of its time high above or far below this standard viewing zone, hiding where traditional surveys aren’t routinely looking.

Researchers plan to decipher if the strange orbits are caused by a prodigal planet or a swarm of rocks. Either way, Holman says “Rubin will image the whole southern sky again and again, so any others hiding in the places earlier surveys skipped are now within reach.”
news.content: بیشتر پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. این کشف جدید ستاره‌ای قبل از آشکار شدن خود به مقداری «فضا» نیاز داشت. دانشمندان مدت‌هاست که با تکیه بر اکتشافات پراکنده و سرنخ‌های غیرمستقیم از حرکات سیارات دیگر، برای نقشه‌برداری منطقه فضایی فراتر از پلوتو تلاش کرده‌اند. اکنون، محققان کشف جدیدی را از رصدخانه Vera C. Rubin Cerroch در مرتفع پلوتون اعلام کرده‌اند. به نظر می رسد یک شی بزرگ در کمربند کویپر - منطقه ای دوردست از اجسام یخی و سنگی در کنار نپتون - یک سیاره کوتوله نامزد جدید باشد. به نام 2026 ED138، کل مدار آن در محدوده فاصله پلوتو از خورشید قرار دارد، اما به تازگی کشف شده است. رصدخانه روبین دارای بزرگترین دوربین دیجیتالی است که تا به حال برای ستاره شناسی ساخته شده است، که قادر است تکه ای از آسمان برابر با 40 ماه کامل را در یک عکس ثبت کند. این تلسکوپ برای اولین بار در ژوئن 2025 نور را دید و تا مارس 2026، این جسم وارد میدان دید خود شد. از آن زمان، این تیم آن را از طریق 30 کشف در 20 شب رصدهای روبین، از 4 مارس تا 11 ژوئیه 2026 ردیابی کردند. معلوم شد که نور یکی از بزرگترین اجرام کشف شده در گذشته از نپتون است که به طور بالقوه با اندازه سایر سیارات کوتوله بالاتر از حد متوسط، مانند Makemake و Haumea رقابت می کند. متیو هولمن، اخترفیزیکدان از مرکز هاروارد-اسمیتسونیان، در 13 اکتبر 2026، هنگام تجزیه و تحلیل مشاهدات روبین با استفاده از نرم افزار توسعه یافته با همکار کوین ناپیر، این شی را مشاهده کرد. تیم با جستجوی داده های قدیمی تر، این شی را در تصاویری از انرژی تاریک آمد.

Bayley may have just given herself new life in WWE. It’s time to give her her flowers and look at her immediate trajectory much differently than a few months ago.

Let’s face it, the negative perception around Bayley for the longest time is that she is fourth among the Four Horsewomen of WWE — Lyra Valkyria even called her that during this recent feud.

And you can certainly make the argument. She has never main-evented WrestleMania, has the lowest number of world titles at four and the closest she’s come to a five-star match was at NXT TakeOver Brooklyn in 2015 with then-Sasha Banks.

She gets far less mainstream exposure than Charlotte Flair and Becky Lynch and her best friend Mercedes Mone went to AEW and went on a belt-collecting spree only rivaled by the legendary Ultimo Dragon.
news.content: بیشتر پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود ببینید. بیلی ممکن است به تازگی در WWE جان تازه ای به خود داده باشد. وقت آن است که به او گل بدهیم و به مسیر فوری او بسیار متفاوت از چند ماه پیش نگاه کنیم. بیایید با آن روبرو شویم، تصور منفی در مورد بیلی برای طولانی‌ترین زمان این است که او در بین چهار اسب‌زن WWE چهارم است — لایرا والکریا حتی او را در این نزاع اخیر به این نام خطاب کرده است. و مطمئناً می‌توانید استدلال کنید. او هرگز رسلمنیا را به عنوان رویداد اصلی بازی نکرده است، کمترین تعداد عناوین جهانی را با چهار عنوان دارد و نزدیکترین عناوین او به یک مسابقه پنج ستاره در NXT TakeOver Brooklyn در سال 2015 با ساشا بنکس آن زمان بود. او به مراتب کمتر از شارلوت فلیر و بکی لینچ و بهترین دوستش مرسدس بنز بود. تنها رقیب Ultimo Dragon افسانه ای است.

Supermodel-turned-media mogul Karlie Kloss is resurrecting Life magazine as a quarterly — with a hefty $45 cover price for its debut issue.

Life, which has weathered decades of financial turmoil, is set to publish its first quarterly edition Nov. 23 — a 250-page issue marking its return to regular print publication for the first time since 2007.

Electric vehicle maker Rivian and software firm Figma are sponsoring the debut issue, which will carry no traditional print ads.

Editors enlisted more than 120 contributors for the edition, themed “Where Are We Now?”

Kloss, the wife of venture capitalist Joshua Kushner and sister-in-law to President Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner, struck a deal through her Bedford Media company in 2024 to relaunch Life.

But the agreement left the publication’s vast historical photography archive in the hands of People Inc, formerly known as Dotdash Meredith.

“What made Life extraordinary was its ability to make the world feel closer,” Kloss told the New York Times in an interview published Wednesday.

“And our responsibility is to preserve and to protect that legacy.”

Kloss told the Times she is focused on developing Life’s business, leaving editorial decisions to the magazine’s staff.

Life’s revival will extend beyond print, with plans for documentary films, events and short-form videos alongside a website and social media presence.

Life debuted in 1936 with a 10-cent issue featuring Margaret Bourke-White’s photograph of Montana’s Fort Peck Dam. Circulation reached roughly 8.5 million copies a week around 1970.

But competition from television and specialized magazines, along with rising printing and postal costs, squeezed the publication’s finances.

Time Inc. shut down the weekly in December 1972 after it racked up losses of roughly $30 million beginning in 1969.

Time Inc. reintroduced Life as a monthly in 1978 but halted regular publication in 2000, when circulation stood at roughly 1.5 million.

A free weekly newspaper supplement followed in 2004, distributed through papers with a combined circulation of about 12 million, before that version was discontinued in April 2007.

Kloss assembled a team that includes creative director Richard Turley, who previously held senior editorial positions at MTV, Bloomberg Businessweek and Interview.

Turley, in turn, recruited former New York Times Magazine editor Hugo Lindgren, former Times photo editor Eve Lyons and former Times pop music editor Caryn Ganz.

Kloss, who previously acquired and relaunched fashion magazine i-D and also holds a stake in W magazine, acknowledged that turning the revived Life into a profitable enterprise won’t happen overnight.

“Building a successful media business takes time, and we’re focused on making measurable progress toward profitability rather than rushing to meet some arbitrary deadline,” she told the Times.

پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. کارلی کلوس، غول رسانه ای تبدیل شده به سوپرمدل، مجله Life را به عنوان یک فصلنامه احیا می کند - با قیمت بالای جلد 45 دلار برای اولین شماره آن. Life، که دهه ها آشفتگی مالی را پشت سر گذاشته است، قرار است اولین نسخه سه ماهه خود را در 25 نوامبر برای چاپ عمومی منتشر کند. از سال 2007 Rivian سازنده خودروهای الکتریکی و شرکت نرم‌افزاری Figma از اولین شماره‌ای حمایت می‌کنند که فاقد تبلیغات چاپی سنتی است. ویراستاران بیش از 120 مشارکت‌کننده را برای این نسخه با مضمون «اکنون کجا هستیم؟» دعوت کردند.
کلوس، همسر جاشوا کوشنر، سرمایه‌دار مخاطره‌آمیز و خواهر شوهر جرد کوشنر، داماد پرزیدنت ترامپ، در سال 2024 از طریق شرکت رسانه‌ای بدفورد خود برای راه‌اندازی مجدد لایف قراردادی منعقد کرد. اما این توافقنامه آرشیو گسترده عکاسی تاریخی نشریه را در اختیار People Inc قرار داد، که قبلاً به نام Dotdash Meredith شناخته می‌شد. کلوس در مصاحبه‌ای با نیویورک تایمز گفت: «آنچه زندگی را خارق‌العاده کرد، توانایی آن در ایجاد احساس نزدیک‌تر به جهان بود.» و مسئولیت ما حفظ و محافظت از این میراث است. کلوس به تایمز گفت که او بر توسعه کسب و کار Life متمرکز است و تصمیمات سرمقاله را به کارکنان مجله واگذار می کند. احیای زندگی فراتر از چاپ خواهد بود، با برنامه هایی برای فیلم های مستند، رویدادها و ویدیوهای کوتاه در کنار یک وب سایت و حضور در رسانه های اجتماعی. Life در سال 1936 با یک شماره 10 سنتی با حضور مارگار آغاز شد.

Ainsley Earhardt vowed to “love and serve” her new husband, Sean Hannity, for the rest of her life while revealing plans to take his last name.

“I am so proud to be his bride and I want to love him and serve him all the days of my life,” Earhardt gushed during her return to “Fox & Friends” on Tuesday, days after tying the knot with the fellow Fox News host.

The newlywed, 50, also revealed that she has already begun signing her text messages as “Mrs. Hannity.”

“I will take his last name for my personal life. I am so proud to be Mrs. Hannity, and I have signed every text, pretty much, that people have sent me, ‘Love, Mrs. Hannity,'” she shared.

However, Earhardt plans to keep her maiden name professionally.

“For TV, I think here at Fox, there’s only room for one Hannity, so I think I will be Ainsley Earhardt forever on TV,” she joked.

During the segment, she also shared new details about their Florida nuptials, which took place on Oct. 24.

“We had a blast,” she said, adding that she felt so much “support” from guests as they tied the knot.

“We were there with so many people from Fox, so many family members, so many friends, and it was everyone in one room that we love most,” Earhardt said. “It was just so special.”

She gushed over her new husband, and said the family was excited for the future.

The blended family includes their children from previous marriages. Hannity has two children — son Sean and daughter Merri — with ex-wife Jill Rhodes, while Earhardt shares pre-teen daughter Hayden with her ex, Will Proctor.

“I’m so in love with that man right there,” she said about Hannity, whom she started dating in 2020.

“He’s the most generous person, he’s so kind, he loves everyone at Fox, he’s just really, really, good,” she shared.

Earhardt and Hannity wed at the Church of Bethesda-by-the-Sea in Palm Beach, Florida, the same place where they got engaged in December 2024.

The wedding guests included many high-profile Washington, DC figures, like Lara Trump and her husband, Eric, as well as former United States Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt.

President Donald Trump and first lady Melania also attended the couple’s pre-wedding celebration at Mar-a-Lago on Friday night.

“Our hearts are overflowing with love and gratitude as we begin this new chapter together as husband and wife,” the newlyweds gushed in a statement.

They called their ceremony “more meaningful than [they] could have ever imagined.”

The couple continued, “Our faith has always been at the center of our relationship, and we truly believe God brought us together. We feel blessed by the outpouring of love and support from the wonderful people in our lives and are excited for the future.”

“Above all,” Hannity and Earhardt concluded, “we are grateful to God for bringing us to this moment and for the beautiful life we will continue to build together.”

Matteo Berrettini has poured fuel on an Italian tennis fire.

During a post-match interview with the ATP 500 Erste Bank Open in Vienna on Monday, the 30-year-old was asked if fellow Italian and “friend” Lorenzo Musetti’s recent Lyon Open title in France serves as “inspiration.”

Berrettini didn’t answer immediately but came out with, “Is it live?” before giving seemingly a restrained response.

Through several pauses and awkward laughs, he said, “It’s okay….I know he worked really hard to come back and I guess he deserved it.”

Berrettini then walked away from the camera.

Oh my goodness! Seems to be genuine beef between Matteo Berrettini and Lorenzo Musetti right now, they used to be very good friends. 👀 pic.twitter.com/i0AzkBcfJs

The awkward response fueled rumors that Musetti, who won his first title since 2022, allegedly hooked up with Berrettini’s ex-girlfriend, Italian dancer Vanessa Bellini.

The two broke up this summer after nearly a year of dating.

As of Wednesday, it seems the 2021 Wimbledon runner-up has unfollowed Musetti on Instagram while the 24-year-old Italian still follows his compatriot. Musetti and his girlfriend, Veronica Confalonieri, still follow each other.

The couple has been together since 2022 and share two sons together, two-year-old Ludovico and near one-year-old Leandro, who was born in November 2025.

Musetti recently posted various photos of the couple while in Tokyo earlier this month.

Both Berrettini and Musetti were members of the 2024 Davis Cup-winning team together. In 2025, Musetti didn’t make himself available for the selection while Berrettini went on to win another tournament title.

This year, Berrettini was not selected for Italy’s Davis Cup squad. Captain Filippo Volandri selected Flavio Cobolli, Luciano Darderi, Andrea Vavassouri, Simone Bolelli and Musetti.

Some have speculated if Berrettini’s snub had to do with the seemingly strained relationship. Volandri cited his selections were based on current rankings.

“The next few weeks leading up to our new Davis Cup adventure will be crucial for me,” he told Italian media per Tennis 365. “My entire staff and I will work to assess each player’s condition to determine their availability, so we can field the best possible lineup.

“We know we have a very strong team, thanks to a wide roster of players, including Matteo Berrettini, Matteo Arnaldi, and Lorenzo Sonego, key players in past seasons.”

Berrettini sits at No. 48 in the rankings while Musetti is No. 26.

The two could meet as early as the semifinals in the Vienna Open in the coming days.

Berrettini has moved on to the Round of 16 and will face Cobolli on Thursday while Musetti is next  taking on Arthur Fery after upsetting American Francis Tiafoe on Wednesday afternoon.

Walmart on Wednesday revealed its annual Thanksgiving meal bundle, which costs just $35 or $3.50 a person — its lowest price yet as the discount retailer attempts to win over cash-strapped Americans.

The Holiday Meal Basket can feed 10 people and includes 26 items – an 18% increase over last year – like a Butterball turkey, stuffing, dinner rolls, mashed potatoes, gravy and pumpkin pie.

New additions include Jiffy corn muffin mix, whipped topping for pie and the ingredients for sweet potato casserole, including sweet potatoes and Jet Puffed mini marshmallows.

Even though it’s more plentiful, the Thanksgiving deal costs 12% less than last year’s bundle, according to Walmart. The Butterball turkey, priced at just 97 cents per pound, boasts the same price tag it had last year — even as Americans complain of stubborn inflation.

“The Holiday Meal Basket has become one of our favorite traditions at Walmart,” David Guggina, president and CEO of Walmart US, said in a statement.

“It brings our purpose to life in such a meaningful way by helping families make the holidays special without stretching their budgets.”

It is available for purchase in stores or online through Christmas Eve Day. Customers can also order the Holiday Meal Basket using curbside pickup, express pickup and scheduled delivery options.

Walmart is offering free express delivery on the deal through Nov. 30.

The full list of items includes: corn muffin mix, whole kernel corn, green beans, mushroom soup, fried onions salad topping, whole russet potatoes, brown gravy mix, frozen pie crusts, whipped topping, pumpkin pure, evaporated milk, rolls, stuffing mix, cranberries, mini marshmallows, sweet potatoes and a frozen whole turkey.

It includes a mix of Walmart’s Great Value brand items and national brands, like Jiffy and Jet-Puffed.

برای خرید در فروشگاه ها یا به صورت آنلاین از طریق شب کریسمس در دسترس است. مشتریان همچنین می‌توانند سبد غذای تعطیلات را با استفاده از گزینه‌های پیکاپ کناری، پیکاپ سریع و تحویل برنامه‌ریزی شده سفارش دهند. news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

An experimental obesity drug significantly reduced breathing interruptions and other symptoms of obstructive sleep disorder in two clinical trials, according to new research published in The New England Journal of Medicine.

Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) affects more than 50 million Americans, and about 80% of cases are undiagnosed, according to the National Sleep Foundation.

The study examined whether retatrutide, an investigational weight-loss drug from Eli Lilly, could help treat OSA in adults who were overweight or obese.

Retatrutide is being evaluated in phase 3 TRIUMPH trials as a potential treatment for obesity and related metabolic conditions. The drug has not been approved by the FDA.

The FDA has warned that unauthorized versions of retatrutide have been illegally marketed and sold online for weight loss.

The two phase 3 randomized trials included 691 adults with moderate-to-severe sleep apnea and a BMI of at least 27. Participants received once-weekly injections of retatrutide at doses of 4, 9 or 12 milligrams, or a placebo, and were followed for 80 weeks.

The trials included 243 participants without type 2 diabetes and 448 with the condition.

Participants who received retatrutide lost between 12% and nearly 20% of their body weight and experienced significantly fewer breathing interruptions than those who received a placebo.

About 68% of participants experienced more than a 50% improvement in OSA symptoms, regardless of whether they had type 2 diabetes.

The study also found that hypoxic burden — the severity and duration of low-oxygen episodes caused by breathing disruptions during sleep — fell by about 75% among participants without type 2 diabetes and 65% among those with the condition.

The researchers concluded that retatrutide led to significantly greater reductions in AHI (breathing interruptions) than a placebo among adults with OSA who were obese or overweight, regardless of whether they had type 2 diabetes.

The researchers noted that retatrutide’s lack of FDA approval was a limitation, and further studies are needed to determine how the drug may affect long-term cardiovascular outcomes.

Study co-author Dr. Virend Somers, a cardiologist and professor of medicine at Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota, told Fox News Digital that while the results were expected, he was surprised by the “magnitude of benefit in patients with type 2 diabetes,” as well as the significant reduction in sleep apnea.

“OSA is often under-diagnosed and under-treated.”

“This is a very exciting time in treating sleep apnea patients,” Somers said.

Sleep apnea is associated with a higher risk of heart attacks, strokes, high blood pressure and atrial fibrillation. In the trial, participants experienced reductions in several cardiovascular risk factors, including systolic blood pressure, LDL cholesterol, systemic inflammation and neck circumference.

“A reduction in these measures would predict whether these patients were at increased cardiovascular risk,” Somers told Fox News Digital.

“In diabetics, blood pressure is a key determinant of future cardiovascular risk, and the fact that we were able to reduce it so significantly was both surprising and exciting.”

Somers said retatrutide also improved several diabetes-related measures.

In participants without diabetes, insulin levels fell by more than 50%. Among those with type 2 diabetes, 40% progressed from diabetes to prediabetes and another 40% no longer met the criteria for diabetes, according to the researcher.

The improvements were largely linked to weight loss, which can lead to better sleep and reduced sleep-related impairment, he said.
news.content: اطلاعات بیشتری از پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید.طبق تحقیقات جدید منتشر شده در مجله پزشکی نیوانگلند، یک داروی آزمایشی چاقی به طور قابل توجهی وقفه های تنفسی و سایر علائم اختلال انسدادی خواب را در دو کارآزمایی بالینی کاهش داد. آپنه خواب انسدادی (OSA) بیش از 50 میلیون آمریکایی را تحت تاثیر قرار داده است و طبق گفته بنیاد Sep، حدود 80 درصد موارد تشخیص داده نشده است. این مطالعه بررسی کرد که آیا retatrutide، یک داروی کاهش وزن تحقیقاتی Eli Lilly، می‌تواند به درمان OSA در بزرگسالان دارای اضافه وزن یا چاق کمک کند. این دارو توسط FDA تایید نشده است. FDA هشدار داده است که نسخه های غیرمجاز retatrutide به طور غیرقانونی به بازار عرضه شده و به صورت آنلاین برای کاهش وزن فروخته شده است. دو کارآزمایی تصادفی‌سازی‌شده فاز 3 شامل 691 بزرگسال با آپنه خواب متوسط ​​تا شدید و BMI حداقل 27 بود. شرکت‌کنندگان هفته‌ای یک‌بار تزریق رتاتتروتاید را با دوزهای 4، 9 یا 12 میلی‌گرم یا دارونما دریافت کردند و 8 شرکت‌کننده به مدت 80 هفته و 4 شرکت‌کننده بدون دیابت نوع 2 را شامل شدند. شرکت‌کنندگانی که retatrutide دریافت کردند بین 12 تا 20 درصد وزن بدن خود را از دست دادند و وقفه‌های تنفسی کمتری را نسبت به افرادی که دارونما دریافت کردند، تجربه کردند. حدود 68 درصد از شرکت‌کنندگان بیش از 50 درصد بهبود علائم OSA را تجربه کردند.

news.originalContent:
Soaring food prices and shrinking incomes force families in Sudan’s capital to borrow money and skip meals.

Khartoum, Sudan – Rasha Abdelaziz Musa works every day for seven hours selling tea. But by the time she finishes for the day at 10pm, she’s still unsure if she has enough to feed her four children.

Musa, 39, is doing her best, but her earnings are increasingly no longer enough to cover soaring food prices in the Sudanese capital.

Her husband, a member of the Sudanese military, has spent more than eight months on the front lines of the country’s war, in which the military has been fighting the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces since 2023. Musa has not heard from him for months, and he has sent no money.

In his absence, Musa has been left to provide for their children, who attend kindergarten, primary and secondary school.

Musa told Al Jazeera that feeding her family costs about 40,000 Sudanese pounds per day ($4 at the parallel-market exchange rate) before accounting for rent, household essentials and other expenses.

Some of the family staples are ful medames, a dish of stewed fava beans, or lentils. When lentils are too expensive, Musa serves taamiya, or falafel, sandwiches.

Prices regularly change, and Musa often ends the day in debt to the traders she gets her food from.

Musa is not alone in struggling to cover her family’s daily expenses.

Ahmed Youssef, 61, supports a family of 12 through his work in a butcher’s shop and as an occasional intermediary in livestock sales. He can earn 90,000 to 140,000 pounds ($9 to $14) when a deal succeeds, but that income is irregular.

He told Al Jazeera that his household spends more than 100,000 Sudanese pounds ($10) daily and his income is no longer enough to support the family.

“One income is no longer enough to cover the family’s needs, and sometimes my older children have to work to help meet expenses,” Youssef told Al Jazeera.

Ali Fadil supports a family of 10. Without a permanent job, he goes to the market each morning to look for work. Some days, the 57-year-old earns enough to buy food, but on other days, he finds no work at all. And yet his daily expenses still reach about 70,000 pounds ($7), with rising prices adding to the financial pressure he faces.

“Sometimes I skip meals so I can pay for school fees or medical costs,” he said. “I also borrow money to meet other obligations.”

A survey of four local markets in the Khartoum State area by Al Jazeera last week found that prices for several essential foods had risen sharply within days, making it increasingly difficult for families to plan their spending.

A kilogramme (2.2.lb) of sugar cost about 10,000 pounds ($1), up from 9,000 pounds ($0.90) two days earlier. A litre (1 quart) of cooking oil rose to 25,000 pounds ($2.50) from 20,000 pounds ($2) while a loaf of bread costs 500 pounds ($0.05), compared with 300 pounds ($0.03) a week earlier.

Lentils cost about 10,000 pounds ($1) per kilogramme, up from 8,000 pounds ($0.80), and rice was priced at 13,000 pounds ($1.30) per kilogramme, up from 10,000 pounds ($1). Powdered milk reached 70,000 pounds ($7) per kilogramme, up from 60,000 ($6) two days earlier.

The Sudanese pound has also continued to weaken. According to exchange rates monitored by Al Jazeera, $1 was trading at 10,050 Sudanese pounds on the parallel market on Friday, compared with 9,500 the previous day.

Official figures offer further evidence of the rising cost of living, particularly in Khartoum and other urban areas.

According to Sudan’s Central Bureau of Statistics, prices across the country were 28 percent higher in September than a year earlier, up from 26 percent in August. Prices rose by 7.5 percent in September alone, more than double the increase recorded the previous month.

Food prices have risen even faster. Across Sudan, food and beverages cost nearly 37 percent more in September than a year earlier, up from an annual increase of about 21 percent in August. In September alone, food prices jumped by more than 17 percent.

The situation was particularly severe in Khartoum State, where prices were nearly 60 percent higher than a year earlier. Prices rose by more than 15 percent in September alone, following an increase of nearly 9 percent in August.

That sharp increase comes as the capital region struggles to recover from widespread destruction caused by the war. Although displaced residents have begun returning and businesses are gradually reopening since the military recaptured the state from the RSF last year, damaged infrastructure and rising transport costs continue to constrain the availability of goods.

The return of residents has also increased demand for essential supplies, further driving up prices. In September, fuel shortages hit the capital as consumption rose faster than supplies could be replenished.

Urban areas have generally been hit harder than rural communities. Food prices in towns and cities were 55 percent higher than a year earlier, up from about 40 percent in August. Overall, prices in urban areas rose by 40 percent over the past year, compared with about 21 percent in rural areas.

The war is the main driver of these increases, disrupting livelihoods and supply chains. According to the World Bank, Sudan’s economy shrank by an estimated 29 percent in 2023 and a further 14 percent in 2024 as the war devastated businesses, disrupted agricultural production and eliminated jobs.

The conflict has also forced millions of people from their homes with nearly 8.9 million people still internally displaced as of April, according to the International Organization for Migration.

Journalist and economic affairs specialist Khalid Teks said Sudan’s economic deterioration began long before the war. Falling oil production after South Sudan’s secession in 2011 worsened conditions as did the depreciation of the pound, cash shortages, international isolation, political conflict and corruption in the years preceding the removal of President Omar al-Bashir in 2019.

Teks said political instability during the power transition undermined Sudan’s economic performance, and deep reforms were not implemented before war broke out in 2023. The conflict devastated infrastructure and productive sectors, depleted savings and disrupted economic activity. The climate has also been a factor. Strong agricultural production in 2024 was followed by concern over limited rainfall this year and possible food shortages after the harvest begins in November.

Teks told Al Jazeera that families increasingly deplete their savings and sell their possessions to cover everyday expenses.

He also pointed to disruptions to remittance channels, which many Sudanese households rely on for financial support.

Teks called for easier humanitarian access, an end to the war, direct support for vulnerable households and low-interest loans for small businesses and craft enterprises.

“The government needs to provide direct support through dedicated funds and the Zakat Chamber, facilitate humanitarian organisations and offer affordable loans for small businesses and vocational activities,” Teks said. “This could help reopen markets and workshops and expand microfinance.
news.content: افزایش قیمت مواد غذایی و کاهش درآمد خانواده‌ها را در پایتخت سودان مجبور می‌کند پول قرض کنند و از وعده‌های غذایی صرف نظر کنند. خارطوم، سودان - راشا عبدالعزیز موسی هر روز هفت ساعت کار می‌کند و چای می‌فروشد. اما تا ساعت 10 شب روز را تمام می کند، هنوز مطمئن نیست که به اندازه کافی برای تغذیه چهار فرزندش دارد یا خیر. موسی 39 ساله تمام تلاش خود را می کند، اما درآمد او به طور فزاینده ای دیگر برای پوشش افزایش قیمت مواد غذایی در پایتخت سودان کافی نیست. شوهر او که یکی از اعضای ارتش سودان است، بیش از هشت ماه را در خط مقدم جنگ این کشور گذرانده است، که در آن ارتش از سال 2023 با نیروهای پشتیبانی سریع شبه نظامی می‌جنگد. موسی ماه‌هاست که از او خبری ندارد و او هیچ پولی نفرستاده است. در غیاب او، موسی برای تأمین مخارج فرزندانشان که به مدرسه ابتدایی و مهدکودک می‌روند، رها شده است. موسی به الجزیره گفت که غذا دادن به خانواده‌اش روزانه حدود 40000 پوند سودانی (4 دلار به نرخ مبادله بازار موازی) قبل از محاسبه کرایه، ملزومات خانه و سایر هزینه‌ها هزینه دارد. برخی از لوازم اصلی خانواده عبارتند از فول مدام، یک غذای لوبیا خورشتی یا عدس. وقتی عدس خیلی گران است، موسی ساندویچ تامیه یا فلافل سرو می کند. قیمت‌ها مرتباً تغییر می‌کند و موسی اغلب روز خود را با بدهی به تاجرانی که غذای خود را از آنها می‌گیرد به پایان می‌رساند. موسی در تقلا برای تأمین مخارج روزانه خانواده‌اش تنها نیست. احمد یوسف، 61 ساله، از طریق کار در قصابی و به‌عنوان یک واسطه گاه به گاه در زندگی، از یک خانواده 12 نفره حمایت می‌کند.

news.originalContent:
The EU has proposed to make Canada its first associate member amid tensions over US tariffs.

Carney backs EU-Canada associate membership amid Trump tariff threats

Canada is set to host a summit with the European Union to bolster bilateral strategic and economic ties as its relations with its southern neighbour, the United States, are in sharp decline.

The summit is scheduled for October 29 to 30 in Canada’s French-speaking city of Montreal, and is expected to focus on closer cooperation on trade, technology, defence, energy, critical minerals, artificial intelligence, research and financial services.

In September, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed opening the door for Canada to become the EU’s first “associate member”; Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney welcomed the move.

This will be the 21st Canada-EU summit and is expected to build on the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), which entered into force in 2017. It eliminates duties on up to 99 percent of all imported goods between the two sides, according to the European Council.

“In Montreal, we will take our partnership to the next level by launching our ‘Alliance for the Future’ to deepen our political, economic and institutional ties even further,” said European Council President Antonio Costa, who will be attending the summit along with Carney and von der Leyen. They are expected to issue a joint statement.

The deepening Canada-EU alignment seems fuelled by US President Donald Trump’s policies, which imposed hefty tariffs on both Canadian and European exports to the US and pushed Canada to look for ways to reduce its economic dependence on the US. Before Trump’s tariffs whipsawed relations, Canada sent nearly 80 percent of its exports to the US.

In August, trade talks between Ottawa and Washington, DC, broke down, and Trump imposed a 50 percent levy on $20bn of Canadian goods, or 5.5 percent of its exports. Canada responded with equivalent tariffs on US steel, dairy, appliances, farm equipment, pulp and paper, and electronics.

Both sides are seeking opportunities that will open more options beyond the world’s largest economy.

“The opportunity is clear. The EU brings market power, research depth, and manufacturing strength. Canada brings abundant energy, critical minerals, world-class capabilities in space, artificial intelligence (AI), and quantum, and one of the world’s strongest banking systems,” Carney’s office said in a statement.

The summit will give the two sides a chance to turn these “complementary strengths into concrete benefits for our peoples,” the statement added.

Vina Nadjibulla, co-founder and CEO of the Centre for Strategic Statecraft, a think tank in Ottawa, Canada, sees benefits and challenges.

“These fields could be beneficial for both sides, and we are likely to see specific announcements during the summit on these sectors,” she told Al Jazeera.

“The main challenge is how quickly the political momentum can turn into specific deals and projects to deliver specific economic results,” she added.

The EU describes Canada as “the only non-European country” taking part in Security Action for Europe (SAFE), the EU’s 150 billion-euro ($167bn) loan programme that supports and expedites defence procurement by EU member states.

The EU concluded its agreement with Canada, allowing it to participate under SAFE, in February, and it gives Canadian firms preferential access and treatment in defence procurements financed by the SAFE Instrument.

Last month, von der Leyen proposed that Canada could become the EU’s first associate member, suggesting a deeper relationship spanning trade, technology, defence and economic security.

Carney later welcomed the proposal’s ambition, describing his goal as a “unique alliance” rather than conventional EU membership.

However, the term “associate member” does not currently exist in EU treaties or its standard enlargement framework, according to the Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS), a Brussels-based think tank.

“The term does not actually matter; what is important is the practical deepening of the relationship and the actual results, no matter what the final term is,” Nadjibulla said.

“This is a partnership not against anyone else, but for our common strength,” von der Leyen said in her address to the European Parliament in Strasbourg last month, which Carney attended, making him the first foreign head of government to attend the annual “State of the European Union” address.

“I do not see that as an anti-US coalition. It is rather about diversification of economic and defence partnerships and building resilience for Canada. It is a continuation of Canadian Prime Minister Carney’s policies to create opportunities. A deeper alliance with Europe is essential to this agenda,” she said.

“President Trump will likely not appreciate this, but it is about Canada having more choices in an unpredictable world,” she added.

Bob Rae, former premier of Ontario and Canada’s ambassador to the United Nations from 2020 to 2025, told Al Jazeera that “President Trump does not control our policy. We have been having long and productive relations with the Europeans for hundreds of years, but Trump chose to treat Canada in a way that does not respect our sovereignty”.

He added that “engaging in conversations with the EU is perfectly normal and is not directed at the US”.

Trump has threatened the European Union with new tariffs over its proposal to make Canada the bloc’s first “associate member”, suggesting the move could be considered hostile to the US.

“If it’s a good intention, that’s fine. If it’s a bad intention, we’ll put very heavy tariffs on Europe,” Trump told reporters in Charlotte, North Carolina, in September.

Trump dismissed the prospect of Canada joining the EU as “laughable” and called the US’s northern neighbour a “terrible trade partner”.

اتحادیه اروپا پیشنهاد کرده است که کانادا را به دلیل تنش‌ها بر سر تعرفه‌های آمریکا، اولین عضو وابسته خود کند.
کانادا قرار است میزبان نشستی با اتحادیه اروپا برای تقویت روابط استراتژیک و اقتصادی دوجانبه باشد زیرا روابط این کشور با همسایه جنوبی خود، ایالات متحده، در حال کاهش شدید است. این اجلاس قرار است 29 تا 30 اکتبر در شهر فرانسوی زبان مونترال کانادا برگزار شود و انتظار می رود بر همکاری نزدیک تر در تجارت، فناوری، دفاع، انرژی، مواد معدنی حیاتی، هوش مصنوعی، تحقیقات و خدمات مالی متمرکز شود. در سپتامبر، رئیس کمیسیون اروپا، اورسولا فون در لاین، پیشنهاد داد که درها را برای کانادا به عنوان اولین "عضو وابسته" اتحادیه اروپا باز کند. مارک کارنی، نخست وزیر کانادا از این اقدام استقبال کرد. این بیست و یکمین اجلاس سران کانادا و اتحادیه اروپا خواهد بود و انتظار می رود بر اساس توافقنامه جامع اقتصادی و تجاری (CETA) که در سال 2017 لازم الاجرا شد، ایجاد شود. به گفته شورای اروپا، این قانون تا سقف 99 درصد از همه کالاهای وارداتی بین دو طرف را حذف می کند. آنتونیو کاستا، رئیس شورای اروپا، که همراه با لی کارنی و فون در اجلاس سران شرکت خواهد کرد، گفت: «در مونترال، با راه اندازی «اتحاد برای آینده» خود برای تعمیق بیشتر روابط سیاسی، اقتصادی و نهادی خود، مشارکت خود را به سطح بعدی خواهیم رساند. انتظار می رود که آنها بیانیه مشترکی صادر کنند. به نظر می رسد تعمیق همسویی کانادا و اتحادیه اروپا توسط رئیس جمهور ایالات متحده، دان تقویت شده است.

news.originalContent:
The central bank increased key rate by a quarter point as soaring energy prices push up inflation.

The Bank of Canada (BoC) has raised its key interest rate for the first time in more than three years and warned that further increases might be needed to prevent soaring energy costs from fueling broader inflation.

Wednesday’s quarter-point hike to 2.5 percent was widely expected, while the bank also ramped up its inflation forecast for 2027 to 3.1 percent from the 2 percent it had predicted in July. Growth this year is set to be 1 percent, higher than the 0.7 percent seen in July.

“With the outlook for inflation substantially higher and the economy showing resilience, an increase in the policy rate is needed to reduce the risk that elevated energy prices could spill over and become generalised inflation,” BoC governor Tiff Macklem said.

“There could be a need to increase the policy rate further, but given uncertainties, we will proceed carefully,” he added.

The annual inflation rate hit 3.2 percent in September, above the bank’s 1 to 3 percent target range, and was driven almost solely by higher energy and energy-related transportation costs.

Macklem said inflation was expected to end the year at 3.5 percent and stay at around 3 percent for most of 2027, before returning close to the 2 percent target by the middle of 2028.

“Governing Council agreed that risks to inflation had increased and there was less scope for monetary accommodation,” Macklem said.

The rate hike was the first since July 2023.

“We don’t expect that core measures of inflation will accelerate as much as the bank fears, particularly if global energy prices ease a little, and as a result we don’t think that the policy rate will need to move above 2.75 percent,” said Andrew Grantham, senior economist at CIBC Capital Markets.

Money markets are pricing in another 25 basis point rate cut in January and see the benchmark rate going up to 3.25 percent by December next year.

Past experience suggests that businesses will increase the cost of products and services in line with changing costs over the next year, increasing overall inflation, Macklem said.

“The combination of higher energy prices and pass-through increases the persistence of inflation,” he said, although he added that there are lingering uncertainties such as the trade rift with the United States and a faster resolution of the conflict in the Middle East.

Economists who opposed a rise said core inflation, which strips out the cost of volatile items, is still hovering at about 2 percent. They also say a rate hike could impede modest economic recovery, given US trade tensions and a weak job market.

Macklem said new US tariffs would slow the economy in the fourth quarter, but expressed confidence that growth should pick up again in 2027 as consumer spending continues, exports pick up and business investment strengthens.

After a robust annualised growth of 3.3 percent in the second quarter, the economy is likely to slow to 2 percent in the third quarter and further down to 0.8 percent in the fourth quarter, the BoC’s new monetary policy report projected.

The report, however, upgraded its gross domestic product (GDP) forecast for next year and the year after to 2 percent from 1.8 percent for both 2027 and 2028, as predicted in July.

Macklem said this additional growth would help absorb the slack, or its unused capacity, in the economy.

The BoC’s next rate decision is on December 9.

news.originalContent:
PM Abiy Ahmed makes the announcement during a Moscow summit as Ethiopia battles armed groups in Tigray and Amhara.

Ethiopia has received 12 Russian Su-35 fighter jets and will also acquire four S-400 air defence batteries, Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has announced.

Abiy made the announcement on X on Wednesday during a visit to Moscow for the two-day Russia-Africa Summit, where Russia is seeking closer security and economic ties with African countries.

The acquisition comes as Ethiopian forces fight renewed battles with rebels in northern Tigray and a separate rebellion in the neighbouring Amhara region.

The prime minister said the warplanes had arrived a year earlier than expected under an existing agreement with Moscow, thanking Russian President Vladimir Putin for helping speed up the delivery.

He gave no date for the arrival of the S-400 batteries, designed to shoot down aircraft and missiles.

Abiy said on Wednesday that the new equipment would strengthen Ethiopia’s ability to “preemptively deter aggression”.

In a second X post later that day, he described the jets as newly deployed and said they would defend Ethiopian airspace.

The announcement is the latest sign of Russia‘s growing military partnership with Ethiopia, following a series of agreements in recent years.

The two governments signed a military cooperation agreement in Addis Ababa in July 2021 aimed at improving the Ethiopian armed forces’ training and technology.

In January, defence publication Janes reported that Ethiopia had displayed newly acquired Russian Yak-130 advanced jet trainers during celebrations marking its air force’s 90th anniversary.

Russia supplied 15 percent of Africa’s imports of major weapons between 2021 and 2025, making it the continent’s third-largest supplier, according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute.

Moscow has sought closer military and economic ties with African countries while facing Western sanctions over its war in Ukraine.

The Russia-Africa Summit, which began on Wednesday, brings African leaders together for talks on trade, investment and security.

The announcement follows a major shift in the fighting in Tigray, where government troops and allied forces entered the regional capital Mekelle on October 4 after fighters from the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) withdrew.

The TPLF, an armed group that previously governed the region, has suffered further territorial losses as government forces advanced into other towns.

Addis Ababa has since appointed a six-month caretaker administration for Tigray, but the fighting has not stopped.

A TPLF commander called for continued resistance in a television broadcast last week, while the group has also claimed attacks against government-aligned troops in northwestern Tigray on Wednesday.

The renewed war has effectively undone a peace agreement signed in Pretoria, South Africa, in November 2022 that ended two years of fighting, which researchers at Belgium’s Ghent University estimate killed about 500,000 civilians.

Government forces are also battling Fano, an Amhara armed group that has been fighting federal troops since 2023.

news.originalContent:
The comment comes as UK and Netherlands pledge extra military support for Kyiv.

European countries will not be included in the next round of talks with Ukraine and the United States planned to take place in Abu Dhabi, according to a top foreign policy aide at the Kremlin.

Interfax news agency quoted Yuri Ushakov, who said the possible participation of European countries was not discussed during a 90-minute phone call on Tuesday among Russian President Vladimir Putin, Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store.

But Stubb offered a different account, telling a meeting of the Nordic Council in Helsinki that European countries would be involved in November’s Abu Dhabi talks.

Speaking at a news conference in the Netherlands on Wednesday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said trilateral talks with Russia and the US would take place from November 6 to November 10 in the United Arab Emirates.

Zelenskyy said Kyiv wanted Europe to also be involved in the talks, adding that unity and stronger pressure on Russia were needed.

His comments came after he met with Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten, who pledged an extra 500 million euros ($556m) for military support to Ukraine this winter to buy drones and other material to strengthen Ukraine’s defences. Zelenskyy is also due to meet Dutch King Willem-Alexander on Wednesday.

Earlier in the day before Zelenskyy’s visit, the Dutch government announced a new support package for Ukraine worth 1.2 billion euros ($1.33bn) over the next three years and a contribution of 40 million euros ($44.5m) by the end of this year to the Ukraine Energy Support Fund.

“Support for recovery and reconstruction can’t wait for a ceasefire. Ukraine needs our help right now – military support but also social and economic assistance,” Sjoerd Sjoerdsma, the Dutch minister for foreign trade and development cooperation, said during a visit to Kyiv on Wednesday.

“However successful you are on the battlefield, it’s also essential that energy systems, hospitals and food production keep ticking over,” he added.

In a separate development, Zelenskyy thanked British Prime Minister Andy Burnham for a newly announced additional support package worth 10 billion pounds ($13.3bn) after a Wednesday morning phone call.

“A truly strong and very timely step – coming right as Russia needs to see and feel that Ukraine will not be left alone to deal with the problems Russia is so eager to escalate,” Zelenskyy wrote on social media.

According to Downing Street, the new British aid package for Ukraine includes 500 million pounds ($665m) in additional military support from the Ministry of Defence “to plug urgent gaps in Ukraine’s air defences this winter”.
news.content: این اظهارات در حالی بیان می‌شود که بریتانیا و هلند حمایت نظامی بیشتری از کیف می‌دهند. به گفته یک دستیار ارشد سیاست خارجی در کرملین، کشورهای اروپایی در دور بعدی مذاکرات با اوکراین و ایالات متحده که قرار است در ابوظبی برگزار شود، شرکت نخواهند کرد. خبرگزاری اینترفکس به نقل از یوری اوشاکوف گفت که در جریان یک تماس تلفنی 90 دقیقه‌ای روز سه‌شنبه میان ولادیمیر پوتین، رئیس‌جمهور روسیه، الکساندر استاب، رئیس‌جمهور فنلاند و یوناس گار استور، نخست‌وزیر نروژ، مشارکت احتمالی کشورهای اروپایی مورد بحث قرار نگرفت. اما استاب در نشست شورای شمال اروپا در هلسینکی گفت که کشورهای اروپایی در مذاکرات ابوظبی در نوامبر شرکت خواهند کرد. ولودیمیر زلنسکی، رئیس جمهور اوکراین روز چهارشنبه در یک کنفرانس خبری در هلند گفت که مذاکرات سه جانبه با روسیه و آمریکا از 6 نوامبر تا 10 نوامبر در امارات متحده عربی برگزار خواهد شد. اظهارات وی پس از دیدار با راب جتن، نخست وزیر هلند بیان شد، که وی متعهد شد 500 میلیون یورو (556 میلیون دلار) اضافی برای حمایت نظامی از اوکراین در زمستان امسال برای خرید هواپیماهای بدون سرنشین و سایر مواد برای تقویت دفاع اوکراین بدهد. زلنسکی همچنین قرار است روز چهارشنبه با ویلم الکساندر پادشاه هلند دیدار کند. پیش از این یک روز قبل از سفر زلنسکی، دولت هلند بسته حمایتی جدیدی را برای اوکراین به ارزش 1.2 میلیارد دلار اعلام کرد.

news.originalContent:
The Hind Rajab Foundation files complaint against an active Israeli soldier, escalating its global accountability campaign.

The Hind Rajab Foundation has filed a criminal complaint in the United Kingdom against Lidor Dafna, an Israeli reservist believed to be visiting the country, over alleged war crimes committed during Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza.

Dafna, who served in the 603rd Combat Engineering Battalion, is accused of participating in the demolition of a flour-producing facility in May 2025 at a time when Israel’s blockade of Gaza was leading to widespread starvation.

The foundation said footage posted by Dafna on social media shows an Israeli military bulldozer demolishing wheat silos in southern Gaza.

The filing is the latest move by the Brussels-based organisation, named after Hind Rajab, a five-year-old girl killed alongside her relatives when Israeli forces fired on their vehicle in Gaza City in January 2024.

By transforming self-published digital content into evidence for criminal complaints, the foundation is testing whether legal systems in other countries may be used to hold Israeli soldiers accountable for alleged crimes.

Natacha Bracq, head of litigation at the foundation, explained the urgency of the UK filing to Al Jazeera.

“If the authorities let him leave, he [Dafna] will go back and commit more crimes. When a state waves a suspect through its airport, knowing what is documented, it is breaching its obligations to prevent and punish genocide.”

Al Jazeera has reached out to the UK’s Metropolitan Police for comment on the case but has yet to receive a response.

For the families of victims in Gaza, the pursuit of justice through international channels is a response to the failure of internal Israeli accountability mechanisms.

Speaking from Gaza, the 45-year-old grandmother and namesake of Hind dismissed internal Israeli military investigations.

“The occupation [Israel] claims that it opens criminal justice or an investigation for their soldiers, [but] we are certainly not very interested in this topic,” she stated. “They just justify their positions to the world, … but actually on the ground, I don’t think anything happens.”

The foundation’s broader goal resonates deeply with families seeking justice for children killed during the war.

“Hind is not the first child in Gaza. Hind means surely there are many crimes like hers and more,” her grandmother added. “We support anyone who speaks in the name of childhood [and always supports] the Palestinian child.”

The Hind Rajab Foundation’s methodology relies heavily on material published by Israeli soldiers themselves.

“Our starting point is simple: Israeli soldiers documented their own crimes. They’ve posted tens of thousands of photos and videos from Gaza and Lebanon on TikTok, Instagram, X and Telegram, often with their faces and names attached,” Bracq said.

This digital footprint requires rigorous processing to become potentially admissible in legal cases.

“Our collection and analysis follow the Berkeley Protocol on Digital Open Source Investigations. Then the real work starts: verification. We geolocate every frame against satellite imagery, matching buildings, roads, water towers, destruction patterns,” Bracq said, noting that investigators then cross-reference military sources to tie a suspect to a documented act.

The Berkeley Protocol, developed by the Human Rights Center  at the University of California in Berkeley and the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights, sets out standards for collecting, verifying, analysing and preserving digital material.

Khaled al-Shouli, an international lawyer registered with the Jordanian Bar Association who represents Palestinian victims before the International Criminal Court (ICC), said social media material could be valuable evidence.

“Its value does not decrease simply because it is a post on the internet, nor does it become decisive simply because it has spread,” al-Shouli said.

He stressed, however, that answering fundamental questions about the source, time and place is essential.

“The crucial difference is the transition from proving the occurrence of the crime to proving the responsibility of a specific person for it as the appearance of a soldier in a place does not alone prove his commission of the crime,” he said.

The foundation’s complaints have prompted authorities in several countries to question Israeli military personnel.

Bracq pointed to a significant breakthrough in Belgium, where a complaint filed by the foundation led federal police to detain and question two Israeli soldiers. Both were subsequently released.

“That arrest matters beyond the two individuals involved. It demonstrated that universal jurisdiction is not a theoretical instrument but one that puts suspects in a police station within hours, and the Belgian federal prosecutor has since referred the case onward to the International Criminal Court,” she stated.

Similar actions have disrupted travel for an Israeli in North America. In Canada, former combat soldier Guy Hochman was detained and interrogated for six hours at Toronto Pearson Airport after a complaint was filed accusing him of war crimes and incitement to genocide. He later said his Canadian visa had been revoked.

“These are ruptures in a system of impunity: the moment Israelis calculate that travelling abroad carries a real legal risk,” Bracq emphasised.

Al-Shouli clarified the legal architecture supporting these moves, distinguishing between national courts and the ICC.

“The Palestinian case relies on a set of matters that fall under the category of territorial jurisdiction over crimes committed in the Palestinian territories and not on absolute universal jurisdiction,” he noted. “This distinction is important because the multiplicity of paths expands the opportunities for accountability and does not leave it hostage to one institution.”

A Hind Rajab Foundation complaint in Brazil highlighted both the potential and the limitations of filing cases against Israelis in the courts of other countries.

In January 2025, Brazilian authorities issued an urgent order to arrest and investigate an Israeli soldier accused of planting explosives and systematically demolishing entire civilian neighbourhoods in Gaza.

While the case attracted international attention, al-Shouli cautioned against overstating its significance. Although a Brazilian judge ordered an investigation after the foundation’s complaint, the Israeli soldier left the country with the assistance of Israeli authorities before he could be detained or questioned.

The case, he explained, highlighted “the gap between opening an investigation and the ability to secure the suspect’s attendance to the justice of the court in practice”.

Political climates heavily influence these legal instruments. Bracq acknowledged that “political will does determine whether a warrant is executed” but countered that “international crimes carry no statute of limitations.” She noted that relentless documentation ensures “no future window of opportunity finds the evidence missing.”

Al-Shouli viewed government transitions pragmatically. “Changing governments opens practical windows for accountability through improving judicial cooperation,” he noted. “But we prefer to describe them as windows to activate the law, not as loopholes in it.”

The foundation is actively expanding its legal efforts beyond individual soldiers to companies and individuals involved in supplying weapons to Israel.

“Our focus has already expanded well beyond front-line soldiers because the strategy must evolve with the genocide itself and with our evidence,” Bracq stated. “We now target the suppliers of the tools of the crime, including companies involved in producing weapons for Israel.”

She cited a recent criminal complaint in Poland against a state-owned TNT producer. “No one gets impunity, from the trigger-puller to the decision-maker to the supplier,” she declared.

For the legal teams, managing the expectations of devastated families remains paramount.

“My professional responsibility begins with not selling false hopes and fake hopes to the victims. It is not permissible for me to tell a family that lost its children that depositing a file has restored its right,” al-Shouli stated. “What we ask for is not sympathy alone but rights that can be proven, claimed and accounted for, and justice will be done.”

“Universal jurisdiction is our instrument, not our objective. Our objective is justice and accountability,” Bracq concluded.

“The generation that posted their own atrocities online now has to live with the knowledge that those posts are forever evidence and that a complaint may be waiting in the next country whose border they cross.”

بنیاد هند رجب علیه یک سرباز فعال اسرائیلی شکایت می کند و کمپین پاسخگویی جهانی خود را تشدید می کند. بنیاد هند رجب شکایتی جنایی علیه لیدور دفنا، یک سرباز ذخیره اسرائیلی که گمان می رود در حال بازدید از این کشور است، به دلیل جنایات جنگی ادعایی که در طول جنگ نسل کشی اسرائیل در غزه مرتکب شده است، در بریتانیا تنظیم کرده است. دفنا، که در گردان مهندسی رزمی 603 ​​خدمت می کرد، متهم است که در تخریب یک مرکز تولید آرد در ماه مه 2025 در زمانی که محاصره غزه توسط اسرائیل منجر به گرسنگی گسترده شده بود، شرکت کرده است. این بنیاد گفت که فیلم منتشر شده توسط Dafna در رسانه های اجتماعی یک نظامی اسرائیلی در جنوب Gazzerat را نشان می دهد. این پرونده جدیدترین اقدام سازمان مستقر در بروکسل به نام هند رجب، دختر پنج ساله ای است که در ژانویه 2024 در جریان تیراندازی نیروهای اسرائیلی به خودروی آنها در شهر غزه در کنار بستگانش کشته شد. ناتاشا براک، رئیس دعوای حقوقی در این بنیاد، فوریت تشکیل پرونده بریتانیا را به الجزیره توضیح داد: "اگر مقامات اجازه دهند او را ترک کند، او [دفنا] برمی گردد و جنایات بیشتری را مرتکب می شود. وقتی دولتی به مظنونی در فرودگاه خود دست تکان می دهد، با دانستن آنچه مستند است، تعهدات خود برای جلوگیری و مجازات نسل کشی را نقض می کند."

news.originalContent:
(Photo by Jeff Swensen/Getty Images)

When the newly inaugurated governor of Ohio, Mike DeWine, was picking someone to run the $640 million Ohio Department of Health in the winter of 2019, he only asked Amy Acton one question: What was your childhood like?

Acton charmed DeWine with her story — the unlikely triumph over a hardscrabble early beginning of homelessness and abuse, which is why DeWine’s top aide had recommended her in the first place. What apparently never came up: the doctor’s resume.

“It was February of 2019, … I got a call out of the blue: ‘The governor really wants to meet you,’” Acton said in public comments in October 2023 about her unlikely rise. “He said to me, ‘tell me about where you grew up. Tell me about your childhood.’ That’s the only question he ever asked.”

“And there’s something about him, I just got very real, because I wanted him to understand the social determinants of health,” she continued. “I said, ‘I had a really rough childhood in Youngstown’ — stuff I didn’t usually share with people in a large way.”

When COVID-19 arrived the next year, Acton, “Ohio’s Anthony Fauci,” had no track record of assessing health data in the scientific literature.

Acton has a medical degree, a master’s in public health and had taught at Ohio State University. But the Democrat’s research portfolio is very thin for someone who specializes in public policy rather than clinical medicine. A search for Acton in PubMed, the repository of medical papers hosted by the National Institutes of Health, turned up just one 2020 study about horse injuries. Nevertheless, Acton issued directives mandating policies restricting the lives of millions.

Seven years later, Acton is seeking to succeed DeWine as governor. She has centered her experience as a public health official as the core of her political identity. Allied groups say Acton is a “doctor, not a politician.” She faces Republican opponent Vivek Ramaswamy. Polls show a tight race.

A panned ad featuring Acton’s estranged mother has once again diverted attention from her pandemic policies to her upbringing.

But while Acton served as the state’s leading health official and as DeWine’s chief medical advisor, Ohio implemented a mask mandate that included indoor and outdoor locations. The state required all children to wear masks in school despite weak evidence for their efficacy in blunting COVID’s already low risk to kids.

An Ohio State research paper found that the pandemic’s hit to some students’ education was roughly equivalent to missing up to a full year’s worth of learning in math and English.

Under Acton’s leadership, Ohio was the first in the nation to announce school closures. In April 2020, Ohio announced schools would remain closed the entire year, while bars were permitted to resume some operations.

She resigned from her position in August 2020 as momentum gathered to ease COVID lockdowns, believing it would violate her Hippocratic Oath to do no harm.

Acton’s campaign did not respond to requests for comment.

Her judgement was “awful … but very much in keeping with the rest of the public health establishment and their recommendations at the time,” said Anish Koka, a cardiologist and health policy commentator, to the Daily Caller News Foundation. “It demonstrates a lack of critical thinking, an inability to analyze primary data, a willingness to follow marching orders. Somebody willing to say the sky is green despite evidence to the contrary. So I’m sure she’ll make an exceptional foot soldier.”

Amy Acton as health director in Ohio ; Shut schools in March (defensible) and then kept them closed for the remainder of the year (indefensible) Shut restaurants Shut gyms Asked churches to cease in person services Banned all visitors to nursing homes for four months Kids, especially poor kids, fell behind. Grandmothers died alone. Suicide rates climbed. Has she ever expressed regret for any of those decisions? https://t.co/bGxNymRrRQ

The single paper Acton co-authored in June 2020 in the American Journal of Emergency Medicine describes a retrospective study showing a decline in the number of people with horse-related injuries at the emergency room.

“Nonfatal horse-related injuries treated in emergency departments in the United States, 1990-2017,” reports a 46% decline in such injuries from 2000 to 2017. The paper concluded that “despite the recent decline in horse-related injuries, these injuries are still common.”

Accordingly, her curriculum vitae (CV) eschews the research publications of a typical university instructor and medical expert and instead highlights positive coverage in the media. She notes that she added a new high-level position at the health department for diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI).

“Acton’s widely acclaimed leadership and inspiring guidance was seen in daily news conferences as COVID exploded in the spring of 2020,” the CV reads.

After the pandemic, Acton incorporated Acton Wellbeing LLC, a consulting business, and began making speeches about COVID. The trademark expires in 2027.

At universities and community centers she delivered a lecture called “The Leader We Wish We All Had Is YOU: Insights from the COVID-19 Pandemic,” an adaptation of a profile by The New York Times in 2020 headlined “The Leader We Wish We All Had.”

We have a responsibility to save lives. We could have waited to close schools, but based on advice from health experts, this is the time to do it. #COVID19 #COVID19OhioReady

In May 2020, Republicans in the state legislature sought to curb Acton’s authority and limit any further stay-at-home orders to 14 days without the approval of a bipartisan committee.

DeWine, a Republican, threatened to veto it, and the proposed curbs never became law.

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) arrested 13 noncitizens accused of voter fraud ahead of the 2026 midterms, according to documents obtained exclusively by the Daily Caller.

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) announced the ICE arrests in connection with alleged voter fraud and other election-related offenses just days before the 2026 midterm elections, according to the documents. (RELATED: ’60 Minutes’ Under Fire After Full DHS Interview Reveals What Was Left On Cutting Room Floor)

In a statement to the Caller regarding the ongoing investigations, DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said, “The patriots of ICE have arrested dozens of non-citizens who illegally voted in American elections.”

“The Trump Administration will not allow illegal aliens to steal the votes of hardworking American citizens,” Mullin added. “American elections are for Americans only.”

The allegations and criminal-history details are based on documents obtained by the Caller, which do not establish that every individual named has been convicted of an election-related offense.

Anti-Fraud AAG Colin McDonald just announced the Trump admin has charged nearly QUADRUPLE the amount of noncitizen voting cases than the Biden admin did… …across his ENTIRE 4 YEARS in office KEEP PROSECUTING! "We’ve charged 50 non-citizens for illegally voting in American elections, with more than a thousand other investigations currently underway." Biden? Only 13 cases in 4 years. MANY more cases are coming from Trump. This is happening because many states are just allowing foreigners to "pinky promise" their are US citizens We’ve allowed them to get Social Security numbers, we’ve let them get taxpayer welfare, and we’ve ALLOWED THEM TO VOTE For both 2026 and 2028 to be saved, America needs secure elections. Prosecute it all and pass the SAVE America Act. https://t.co/EDewzmgjhv

Among the cases highlighted by DHS was Juan Carlos Matute-Hernandez, a Honduran national accused of illegally voting in the 2026 election. His record includes an arrest for driving offenses, according to the agency.

Aden Hassan Aden, a Somali national, was accused of illegally voting in the 2020 election. His criminal history includes convictions for domestic violence, drug possession, and larceny, according to documents.

Several other cases involved alleged illegal voting in the 2024 election, including Arturo Salazar Garcia, a Mexican national, and Jaimie Sosa-Sardina, a Cuban national. Sosa-Sardina’s criminal history includes convictions for selling cocaine, battery, and resisting an officer, according to the department.

Marva Marie Cook, a German national accused of illegally voting in the 2022 election, has a criminal history that includes a larceny conviction, the agency said.

Acting ICE Director David J. Venturella told the Caller that the investigations involved coordination with other law enforcement agencies. “These arrests, carried out in coordination with our federal, state and local law enforcement partners, are the result of careful, methodical investigations,” Venturella said.

“American elections must be conducted in accordance with the law, and allegations of illegal voting deserve our undivided attention,” Venturella added. “When the facts support criminal charges, we pursue them. Every eligible voter deserves an election process that follows the law.” (RELATED: EXCLUSIVE: ICE Nabs Violent Illegal Who Came Back After 2 Deportations)

Other individuals accused of illegally voting in the 2024 election include Braulio Osiel Zapata Perez, a Nicaraguan national whose record includes an arrest for driving under the influence, and Mai Tran, a Vietnamese national whose criminal history includes convictions involving fraud, drug possession, selling cocaine, burglary, larceny, and the illegal use of credit cards, according to the documents.

Jose Luis Matute Chaviel, a Venezuelan national, was accused of illegally voting in the 2024 election. His record includes charges involving driving under the influence and cocaine possession, the agency said.

Phath Vorn, a Cambodian national, was accused of illegally voting in the 1992 election. His criminal history includes convictions for assault with intent to murder, assault with a dangerous weapon, and weapons possession, according to the department.

The documents further highlight the case of Axel Bemjarmin Alarcon Duarte, a Guatemalan national accused of illegally voting in a federal election. He has also been charged with driving under the influence, assault and battery on a family member, and shoplifting.

Darwin Yoel Zelaya-Orellana, a Honduran national, was accused of illegally voting in a 2026 election. His criminal history includes a conviction for a third-degree sex offense, the department said.

Servando Alejandro-Torres, a Mexican national, was accused of illegally voting in the 2024 election. His record includes convictions for disorderly conduct and bail jumping, as well as driving-under-the-influence charges, according to the agency.

Jairo Ivan Vazquez Montano, a Mexican national accused of illegally voting in the 2022 election, has a criminal record that includes arrests involving kidnapping, driving under the influence, and another traffic offense, the department said. (RELATED: DOJ Investigating Corey Lewandowski Over Alleged Profiteering At DHS)

In recent months, DHS has taken additional steps to safeguard election integrity. In June, DHS directed ICE to enforce stricter penalties, including deportation, for noncitizens who illegally vote in U.S. elections.

In July, Secretary Mullin warned state election officials that tens of thousands of noncitizens were registered to vote.

The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) released its 2026 Election Infrastructure Security Plan in September.
